origin.description: Interval of parameter values whose profile likelihood exceeds a limit.

arguments.name: like
arguments.text: Matrix with the parameter in column 1 and the likelihood in column 2.

arguments.name: lim
arguments.text: Likelihood limit. The interval covers parameters whose likelihood is strictly above this value.

origin.details: Written for practicals 10.1 and 10.2 of Davison and Hinkley (1997). The endpoints are interpolated only for a unimodal likelihood. The formula is lm(y ~ x + x^2). In that formula ^ is a crossing operator, so the fit has no squared term and an interior endpoint is NA. A likelihood that is still above the limit at an end of the grid gives -Inf or Inf. One point above the limit, or none, is an error.
origin.value: A length-2 numeric vector, the lower and upper endpoints, with names removed.
origin.example:
theta <- seq(64, 82, length.out = 11)
L <- -((theta - 77)^2)
like <- cbind(theta, L)
print(lik.CI(like, -200))
print(lik.CI(like, -10))

translation.description: Interval of parameter values whose profile likelihood exceeds a limit.

arguments.name: like
arguments.text: Two-column array. Column 1 is the parameter and column 2 is the likelihood.

arguments.name: lim
arguments.text: Likelihood limit. The interval covers parameters whose likelihood is strictly above this value.

translation.details: The comparison, the messages, and the missing interior endpoints follow the installed function. x^2 does not add a square, so an interior endpoint is NaN. A likelihood still above the limit at an end of the grid is -inf or inf.
translation.value: A length-2 array, the lower and upper endpoints.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from boot.profile import lik_ci

theta = np.linspace(64, 82, 11)
like = np.column_stack([theta, -((theta - 77) ** 2)])
print(lik_ci(like, -200))
print(lik_ci(like, -10))
